intuition.title: Combining phosphorus sources with different reactivities
intuition.text: The authors use rapidly reacting P(SiMe3)3 with slower P(SiPh3)3 to help separate nucleation from subsequent growth. They interpret the slower precursor as a reservoir that can continue supplying growth material. This is a mechanistic interpretation supported by their comparisons, not a direct measurement of instantaneous monomer concentration.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.
source_locators: Main PDF p.4 / printed p.1737, Results and Discussion
Main PDF pp.6–7 / printed pp.1739–1740, Figure 6 and discussion

intuition.title: Why nucleation control alone is insufficient
intuition.text: The authors conclude that separating nucleation and growth in time does not by itself ensure a narrow size distribution in covalent InP. Monomer consumption during growth also matters. Their optical, TEM and simplified spherical-model comparisons support this interpretation; the model outputs remain calculated quantities.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.

general_background.title: Destabilizing a particle dispersion
general_background.summary: An antisolvent can solvate a particle's ligand shell less favourably than the original dispersion medium. Reduced solvation can weaken colloidal stability and allow particles to aggregate and separate from the liquid, depending on the ligands and solvent mixture.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: Solvent and transport
general_background.summary: A solvent carries dissolved species and transports heat through a reaction or dispersion. Solubility, viscosity and molecular interactions affect how precursors and ligand-coated particles move and mix.
